title: Consuming JSON APIs
learning_outcomes: Explain what consuming json apis contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: request parameters.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: API integrations cross a network boundary where responses can be slow, malformed, unauthorized, duplicated, or unavailable. Check status and content, set timeouts, and make retries and webhook processing safe to repeat. In this lesson, focus on request parameters; then compare it with authorization headers. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use consuming json apis when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: API integrations cross a network boundary where responses can be slow, malformed, unauthorized, duplicated, or unavailable. Check status and content, set timeouts, and make retries and webhook processing safe to repeat. For consuming json apis, begin with request parameters. Also distinguish authorization headers; json request bodies; decoding responses. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
